    Almost-split morphisms under equivalence #

    An ordinary categorical equivalence preserves right and left almost-split morphisms and their minimality. The proof uses essential surjectivity to pull an arbitrary test object back across the equivalence and full faithfulness to reflect splittings.

    This is the covariant companion of the anti-equivalence argument in QuotientSubmoduleEquidistribution.RepresentationTheory.AlmostSplitDuality; only the two transport lemmas required by the support-algebra passage are included here.

    source
    theorem QuotientSubmoduleEquidistribution.IsRightAlmostSplit.map_equivalence {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u'} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v', u'} D] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsRightAlmostSplit f) (E : C ≌ D) :
    IsRightAlmostSplit (E.functor.map f)

    A right almost-split morphism remains right almost split after applying an equivalence.

    source
    theorem QuotientSubmoduleEquidistribution.IsRightAlmostSplit.of_map_fully_faithful {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u'} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v', u'} D] (F : CategoryTheory.Functor C D) [F.Full] [F.Faithful] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsRightAlmostSplit (F.map f)) :
    IsRightAlmostSplit f

    Right almost-splitness is reflected by a fully faithful functor.
